page.layout: Printed page 236 at top left, with running head "ANTIDOTUM, &c." at top right. Main text block at top right: an italic-heavy paragraph continuing from the previous page. Below it, centred: a dedication in larger italic and roman type, with an asterisk reference in the left margin and a line "FINIS." below. Museum stamp at the bottom, not transcribed.

main_text.p: Quasi enim sub hoste quem profternit moritur, qui de culpa, quam superat, elevatur. Sic ille. Quæ autem detestabilior superbia esse potest, quàm quæ non modò Gratiam de superan-dis vitiis nimis sibi vendicat, verùm etiam Gloriam vitæ æternæ ex æqualitate justitiæ exi-git, & deberi sibi ex condignitate statuit, pertinaciterque defendit
Autori omnis operis boni, Soli Deo, {*}à Quo, per Quem, & ad Quem sunt omnia, sit Glo-ria in secula.Rom.11. 36.

page.notes: The text is rather faded; "profternit" and "debori" are as far as I can read them, and the italic/roman split in the first sentence is uncertain. "Sic ille." may be roman rather than italic. The paragraph ends at "defendit" with no visible full stop. A small "242" appears at top right beside the running head; it may be a stray number, so I have not recorded it as a page number. A faint mark at bottom right is a digitiser or shelf mark and is left out. The museum stamp is left out.
